The question I kept coming back to while moderating the discussion at the #HLPF2026 High-level Thematic Event on Accelerating Energy System Innovation and Transition for Equity and Resilience was a simple one:
 
Can our institutions evolve as quickly as our technologies?
 
The numbers tell an interesting story. 92% of the world's population now has access to electricity, yet the pace of electrification has slowed: Reaching universal access by 2030 will require progress at more than three times today's rate.
 
Meanwhile, the transition itself is accelerating. Renewables now generate over 30% of global electricity, solar and wind consumption has increased fivefold in the past decade, and AI could save the power sector up to USD 110 billion every year through smarter planning and operations.
 
If we have technology, innovation, what is the real bottleneck? Are we still treating electricity as the end goal, when it should be the beginning of economic transformation? 
 
I was pleased to moderate the panel discussion at today's #HLPF2026 High-level Thematic Event on Accelerating Energy System Innovation and Transition for Equity and Resilience, bringing together experts from the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), Sustainable Energy for All (SEforALL), the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the World Resources Institute (WRI).
 
The discussion reinforced that stronger institutions, better planning, bankable investment pipelines and financing models that reduce risk are what will determine whether innovation reaches the countries and communities that need it most. Unlocking nearly USD 1 trillion in annual private investment in emerging and developing economies will require around USD 80–100 billion of concessional finance each year.
 
My thanks to GEIDCO(Global Energy Interconnection Development and Cooperation Organization) and all the partners for convening this timely dialogue, to our excellent panelists, and to everyone who contributed to such a thoughtful exchange.
 
What innovation - technological, financial or institutional - will have the greatest impact on accelerating SDG 7?
